# Section documentation for [STACK-Maxima](../index.md) /linearalgebra

Matrix operations, predicates and equation-display functions provided by STACK.
They are available in question variables, answer tests and feedback without
loading `matrix.mac`. That file remains available as a compatibility include and
continues to enable the convenience vector aliases.

The reference below covers extracting, replacing and scaling matrix entries.
The subdirectories document matrix predicates and the display of linear systems.


---


## columnscale(M,i,alpha)<a id='columnscale'></a>

Scales column i of matrix A by alpha.
A companion to columnop and columnswap.
C_i <- alpha*C_i



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | matrix | The matrix whose column you are scaling |
| i | integer | The column you are scaling |
| alpha | number | The amount you are scaling the column. |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| matrix | C_i <- alpha*C_i |


---


## diag_entries(M)<a id='diag_entries'></a>

Extracts the diagonal of a matrix as a list. For a rectangular matrix,
the list has length `min(m,n)`. Non-matrix input is returned in a singleton list.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | matrix | An mxn matrix |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| list | The diagonal entries of M as a list |


---


## diagmatrix_like(d,m,n)<a id='diagmatrix_like'></a>

Construct a diagonal matrix of size m by n with diagonal given as a list
Similar to native function diag which builds a block diagonal matrix, but instead
is intended for numerical diagonals of rectangular matrices.
Intended use case is to extend a reduced SVD into a full SVD
If the whole diagonal does not fit in an mxn matrix, then it truncates d.
If d is not long enough to fill an mxn matrix, remaining diagonal entries are set to 0.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| d | list | the list of diagonal entries, which may be symbolic. |
| m | positive integer | The number of rows in the desired matrix |
| n | positive integer | The number of columns in the desired matrix |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| matrix | A mxn matrix with d as the diagonal |


---


## diagonal(M)<a id='diagonal'></a>

Take the diagonal of a matrix, leaving the remaining entries = 0.
The matrix may be rectangular. Non-matrix input is returned unchanged.
This uses `genmatrix`, which requires positive row and column counts.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | matrix | An mxn matrix |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| matrix | The same matrix with all off-diagonal entries set to 0 |


---

A companion to rowop and rowswap.

| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | matrix | The matrix whose row you are scaling |
| i | integer | The row you are scaling |
| alpha | number | The amount you are scaling the row. |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| matrix | R_i <- alpha*R_i |

## setcolmx(c,i,M)<a id='setcolmx'></a>

Replace column i of matrix M with c.
If c is a list or a matrix, replace the column exactly. Nothing will happen if c does not conform.
If c is a number, fill column i with the value c.
Companion to setelmx



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| c | number, list or matrix | the replacement column (or value that will be repeated in the column) |
| i | integer | the index of the column that will be replaced |
| M | matrix | the matrix whose column is being replaced |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| matrix | The matrix M with column i replaced by c. |


---


## setdiagmx(L,M,[_k])<a id='setdiagmx'></a>

Replace diagonal k of matrix M with L.
If L is a list, replace the diagonal exactly.
If L is too short to fill the diagonal, then any remaining diagonal entries are untouched
If L is too long for the diagonal, then only the first l entries of L are used, where l is the length of the diagonal.
If L is a number, fill the diagonal with the value L.
If the optional argument k is given, then choose the kth diagonal. For example, setdiagmx(L,M,1) will adjust the values one entry above the primary diagonal.
Companion to setelmx



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| L | number or list | the replacement diagonal (or value that will be repeated in the diagonal) |
| M | matrix | the matrix whose diagonal is being replaced |
| _k | integer | optional diagonal offset; defaults to zero. |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| matrix | The matrix M with diagonal k replaced by L. |


---


## setrowmx(r,i,M)<a id='setrowmx'></a>

Replace row i of matrix M with r.
If r is a list or a matrix, replace the row exactly. Nothing will happen if r does not conform.
If r is a number, fill row i with the value r.
Companion to setelmx



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| r | number, list or matrix | the replacement row (or value that will be repeated in the row) |
| i | integer | the index of the row that will be replaced |
| M | matrix | the matrix whose row is being replaced |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| matrix | The matrix M with row i replaced by r. |


---


## tril(M)<a id='tril'></a>

Take the lower triangular part of a matrix, leaving the remaining entries = 0.
The matrix may be rectangular. Non-matrix input is returned unchanged.
This uses `genmatrix`, which requires positive row and column counts.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | matrix | An mxn matrix |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| matrix | The same matrix with all entries above the diagonal set to 0 |


---


## triu(M)<a id='triu'></a>

Take the upper triangular part of a matrix, leaving the remaining entries = 0.
The matrix may be rectangular. Non-matrix input is returned unchanged.
This uses `genmatrix`, which requires positive row and column counts.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | matrix | An mxn matrix |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| matrix | The same matrix with all entries below the diagonal set to 0 |
